title: 2010 AMC 10B Problem 8
statement: A ticket to a school play costs \(x\) dollars, where \(x\) is a whole number. A group of \(9\)th graders buys tickets costing a total of \(\$48,\) and a group of \(10\)th graders buys tickets costing a total of \(\$64.\) How many values for \(x\) are possible?

solutions.text:
Note that \(x\) must divide both \(48\) and \(64,\) which means that it must divide their greatest common divisor.

The greatest common divisor of \(48\) and \(64\) is \(16,\) which means \(x\) divides \(16.\)

\(16\) has \(5\) factors, namely all the powers of \(2\) up to \(16.\)

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: The ticket price must divide both totals
